title: Autoscaler safety-window fix to prevent late scale-ups causing reserved-pool burst shortfalls
creator: Lina Chen
description: Production escalation from two customers experiencing denied requests and token exhaustion in reserved pools during sustained bursts. Investigation found the autoscaler was not issuing timely scale-ups due to a cooldown/safety-window race with queue-length sampling; a separate bug allowed burst credits to be decremented twice during a retry path, accelerating pool depletion. This ticket tracked the hotfix, runbook updates, and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
investigation_notes: 03/01 06:12 UTC - Pager triggered: tenant ACME-ML saw a spike in 503s from dedicated pool despite apparent available capacity in the cluster.
03/01 06:20 UTC - Oncall captured allocator traces and autoscaler logs; observed scale decision suppressed by safety_window flag set after recent downscale.
03/01 07:05 UTC - Correlated with token-accounting logs: 'burst_credit_decrement' executed twice for ~1200 requests in 6m during retry loop in frontend gateway.

03/01 08:10 UTC - Reproduced race locally by simulating back-to-back downscale then surge; autoscaler cooldown suppressed immediate scale-up for configured 30s safety window while queue backlog spiked.
03/02 11:30 UTC - Confirmed that the safety-window uses a metric sample timestamp that may be stale if controller restarts during monitoring windows, causing an extra effective cooldown.
03/03 09:40 UTC - Customer mitigation: increased tenant burst quota and temporary fallback to hosted fallback model for latency-sensitive routes while patch deployed.
03/04 13:00 UTC - Root cause hypothesis validated in staging with load tests and deterministic fault injection.
03/05 18:20 UTC - Hotfix branch created and code review started (see code_prs).
root_cause: Two independent issues combined to cause the outage: 1) Autoscaler's safety-window/cooldown logic could be extended incorrectly after controller restarts because it relied on sampled timestamps rather than monotonic event counters, delaying scale-ups during immediate post-downscale bursts. 2) Frontend retry path mistakenly performed an extra burst-credit decrement on transient failures, causing faster-than-expected reserved-pool depletion. The combination produced temporary token exhaustion even though physical GPU headroom existed.
fix_summary: Deployed a two-part hotfix: (A) Change autoscaler cooldown to use an idempotent monotonic scale-event counter and add metric smoothing of queue_length to avoid reacting to transient noise; reduce safety window from 30s to 8s for burst-prone pools with canary flag. (B) Patch frontend retry path to make burst-credit decrement atomic and only on final success path; add a safety check to prevent negative balance. Added unit tests and e2e load test harness that simulates downscale-then-spike scenarios.

https://github.com/redwood-inference/frontend/pull/2291 - frontend: atomic burst-credit decrement and retry guard
runbook_changes: Updated 'reserved-pool-depletion' runbook: add immediate mitigation step to temporarily route latency-critical routes to hosted fallback and instructions to raise tenant burst quota for affected customers.
Added 'diagnose-scale-delay' checklist with specific log queries and Grafana panels to check autoscaler event counter and queue-length trend.
test_plan: Unit tests for atomic decrement, integration test for retry path, staging e2e: simulated downscale followed by 2x burst for 10 minutes across 5 tenants, measure time-to-scale and token-accounting correctness. Added nightly regression that runs the downscale+spike scenario on dedicated CI cluster.
rollout_plan: Canary deploy autoscaler change to 3% of dedicated clusters for 2 hours with synthetic spike load. If graphs show successful scale-ups within target SLO (scale latency < 6s) and no negative balances, expand to 20% then 100% over 24 hours. Frontend patch rolled together in same canary to avoid mismatch.
rollback_plan: If canary shows increased instability or incorrect accounting, revert PRs and toggle canary flag. Pre-approved rollback playbook in runbook with steps to re-route traffic off impacted clusters and manually credit affected tenant pools.
